classification.theory_summary: Proposes that Mallworld resembles a mall because malls hold happy/nostalgic memories for many people (shopping with family, hanging out with friends, arcade/Orange Julius, first jobs, independence, driving after getting a license). Asks what future generations will dream of as malls decline.
classification.skip_reason: Post is a speculative theory about why the shared dream setting is a mall; it does not describe a specific dream episode, locations visited in-dream, or concrete phenomenological details beyond general references.

meta.author_theory: Mallworld may be more than a random dream: an ethereal terminal/subconscious waypoint for collective minds. The mall form is attributed to positive nostalgic associations with malls (family shopping, friends/arcade, Orange Julius, first jobs/independence, first solo driving).

extraction.extraction_notes: No first-person dream narrative or in-dream scene description. Mentions of malls/arcades/Orange Julius are used as examples of waking-life memories, not described as dream locations.
